# Operations: build rules

Apply these rules while you build. Domains or criteria whose `applies_if` flags are false in `.quality/project.json` do not apply to this project. Before you call a task done, check your work against the criteria of the domains you touched: each one must be true and verifiable.

If a stack module of the quality pack is installed (qp-nextjs, qp-node-api, qp-vps, qp-expo, qp-capacitor, qp-tauri, qp-electron), its rules skill adds stack-specific rules on top of these.

## Infrastructure (INF)

Server configuration, process management and automatic restart.

Applies when: Hosted on a team-managed server (VPS, dedicated).

Rules:

- Server configuration described in versioned files (Docker Compose, Nginx config, PM2 ecosystem), never only by hand.
- Every process restarts automatically after a crash and on server reboot.
- Firewall on: only required ports open; database and Redis not exposed publicly.
- SSH by key only, automatic security updates.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] INF-01: Database, Redis and admin ports not publicly exposed. Check: External port scan; bindings on 127.0.0.1 or internal Docker network.
- [major] INF-02: Automatic restart after crash and after reboot. Check: restart: unless-stopped, pm2 startup and pm2 save, or a systemd unit.
- [major] INF-03: Server configuration versioned and reproducible. Check: Rebuild the environment from the repo and a .env.
- [major] INF-04: HTTPS everywhere with automatic certificate renewal. Check: HTTP to HTTPS redirect; expiry date and auto-renewal.
- [minor] INF-05: Hardened server access (SSH keys, firewall, automatic updates). Check: PasswordAuthentication no, ufw or equivalent, unattended-upgrades.
- [minor] INF-06: Resource limits and log rotation. Check: Memory limit per container or process; logs that do not fill the disk.

## Deployment (DEP)

Release and rollback.

Rules:

- Deploy through one command or pipeline, never by copying files by hand.
- Every deployed version is identifiable (Git tag, build number) and the previous one stays available.
- Write and test the rollback procedure before you need it.
- Deploy to staging first when the change touches data, payments or authentication.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] DEP-01: A rollback procedure exists and has been tested. Check: Rollback document and date of last trial.
- [major] DEP-02: Automated and reproducible deployment. Check: Single script or pipeline; no undocumented manual step.
- [major] DEP-03: Tests and build gate production releases. Check: The pipeline stops if typecheck, lint, tests or build fail.
- [major] DEP-04: Migrations applied safely at deployment (only if: has_db). Check: Migration and code order compatible; backup before destructive migration.
- [minor] DEP-05: Deployed version identifiable and visible. Check: Git tag or hash exposed in a health endpoint or the logs.
- [minor] DEP-06: Staging environment separate from production. Check: Separate database, secrets and domain.

## Monitoring (MON)

Monitoring, error logs and alerts.

Applies when: The project has a server or API or Public pages meant to be found on the web.

Rules:

- Send server and client errors to a tool (Sentry, GlitchTip…) with the version and no personal data.
- Expose a health endpoint and monitor it from outside (Uptime Kuma, Better Stack…).
- Structured logs (JSON) with a level and a request ID.
- An alert must reach a channel that is read (email, phone), and only for what needs action.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] MON-01: A site outage triggers an alert someone receives. Check: External monitoring configured; test alert received.
- [major] MON-02: Server and client errors reported to a tracking tool. Check: SDK configured, test error visible with version and trace.
- [major] MON-03: Health endpoint that checks critical dependencies (only if: has_backend). Check: /health responds and checks database and Redis.
- [minor] MON-04: Structured, timestamped logs kept for a defined period (only if: has_backend). Check: JSON format, level, request ID, rotation.
- [minor] MON-05: Alert before domain and certificate expiry, and on disk space. Check: Monitoring of expiry dates and disk.

## Backups (BAK)

Automated backups, tested restore and recovery.

Applies when: Database or User file uploads.

Rules:

- Automatic daily backup of the database and user-uploaded files.
- 3-2-1 rule: at least one copy off the production server, with another provider or region.
- Backups encrypted and kept for a defined period.
- Test a full restore at least once a quarter and record how long it takes.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] BAK-01: Automatic backup of the database and user files. Check: Scheduled job and latest backup less than 24 h old.
- [BLOCKER] BAK-02: A full restore has been tested. Check: Date and duration of the last successful restore on a separate environment.
- [major] BAK-03: At least one copy off the production server. Check: External destination (object storage, other server) checked.
- [major] BAK-04: Backup failure raises an alert. Check: The backup script alerts on failure or absence.
- [minor] BAK-05: Encrypted backups with a defined retention period. Check: Encryption and rotation configured.
- [minor] BAK-06: Written recovery plan (who does what, in which order). Check: Recovery document with acceptable downtime and data-loss targets.
